title: Transitivity of SLₙ(ℤ) on Primitive Vectors

problemStatement.formal: \forall\, v \in \mathbb{Z}^n \text{ with } \gcd(v_1,\dots,v_n)=1,\ \exists\, U \in \mathrm{SL}_n(\mathbb{Z}) \text{ such that } U \cdot v = e_1 = (1,0,\dots,0)^{\top}.
problemStatement.plain: The parent proof shows that for coprime integers a, b there is a 2×2 integer matrix of determinant 1 sending (a,b) to (1,0). This problem asks for the n-dimensional analogue: given any primitive integer vector v = (v_1,…,v_n) (coordinates with gcd 1), construct an n×n integer matrix U of determinant 1 — an element of SLₙ(ℤ) — carrying v to the first standard basis vector e_1 = (1,0,…,0). Equivalently, SLₙ(ℤ) acts transitively on primitive integer vectors, so every primitive vector extends to a ℤ-basis of ℤⁿ.
whyMatters: Transitivity of SLₙ(ℤ) on primitive vectors is the statement that a primitive vector always completes to a unimodular basis of ℤⁿ — foundational for lattice arithmetic.
It underlies Smith normal form, the structure theory of finitely generated abelian groups, and the reduction theory of quadratic forms in n variables.
The n=2 case is the arithmetic seed of the modular group SL₂(ℤ); the general case is the natural next rung, tying Bézout's identity directly to lattice geometry.
An effective (computable) construction gives a reusable reduction tool inside Mathlib, beyond a pure existence argument.

proven: n=2 case: the parent proof bezout-identity-oq-01-oq-02 builds the explicit unimodular 2×2 reduction matrix, proves U·(a,b)=(gcd,0), det U = 1 for gcd ≠ 0, and packages coprime pairs as SL₂(ℤ) elements.
Bézout's identity via Mathlib's Int.gcd_eq_gcd_ab / Int.gcdA / Int.gcdB drives each 2-variable reduction step.
Classical existence over PIDs (a primitive vector extends to a basis) is standard, though not in the effective SpecialLinearGroup form this problem targets.
open: An effective Lean construction of U ∈ SLₙ(ℤ) (not merely existence) carrying an arbitrary primitive v to e_1, generalizing bezoutMatrix to n coordinates.
A clean induction/recursion on n keeping the determinant exactly 1 at every step, matching the parent's sign convention.
Packaging the result as transitivity of the Matrix.SpecialLinearGroup (Fin n) ℤ action on primitive vectors in Mathlib-idiomatic form.
knownResults.goal: Formalize in Lean 4 over Mathlib that every primitive v ∈ ℤⁿ admits U ∈ SLₙ(ℤ) with U·v = e_1, via an explicit recursion that reduces the n-coordinate case to the parent's 2-coordinate bezoutMatrix, machine-verified with no new axioms.

insights: Primitivity of an integer vector v is cleanly captured coordinate-free as: ∃ dual w with w ⬝ᵥ v = 1. This dot-product form is manifestly SLₙ(ℤ)-invariant, unlike the gcd-of-entries phrasing.

SLₙ(ℤ) preserves primitivity in BOTH directions: if w ⬝ᵥ v = 1 then (w ᵥ* ↑ₘA⁻¹) ⬝ᵥ (↑ₘA *ᵥ v) = 1, because ↑ₘA⁻¹ * ↑ₘA = 1. This is the exact invariant the transitivity action must respect — the necessity half of the transitivity characterization.

The Euclidean-descent generators are Mathlib transvections: transvection i j c = I + c·Eᵢⱼ (i≠j) has det 1 (det_transvection_of_ne), so it packages directly into SLₙ(ℤ); its action adds c·vⱼ to vᵢ (Function.update).

CONVERSE ALREADY PROVED (Transitive.lean, unverified): working in the Fin (2+m) index convention makes 2+(m+1) DEFINITIONALLY (2+m)+1, so Fin.cons / embedOne / headBlockN types line up with no transport. Induction template per step: embedOne of the SL₍₂₊ₘ₎ gcd-reducer of the tail clears coords 2…n against coord 1 (giving (v₀,g_tail,0,…,0)); then headBlockN of the SL₂ gcd-reducer of (v₀,g_tail) clears coord 1 against coord 0. Single content bridge cons_gcdForm repackages the Fin.cons output as the Fin.append input. Primitivity collapses g to 1 via g ∣ (w ⬝ᵥ v)=1 ⇒ Int.eq_one_of_dvd_one. This is the arbitrary-n generalization of the parent bezoutMatrix reduction.

The converse (sufficiency) direction of SLn(Z)-transitivity on primitive vectors — every primitive v is SLn(Z)-equivalent to a unit multiple of a basis vector — holds in EVERY dimension by strong induction on the l1 measure sum_k |v_k|, no analytic input needed (elementary Euclidean descent).

The termination measure is sum_k (v k).natAbs; a single transvection T_{i,j}(-(v i / v j)) replaces the pivot v i by v i % v j, and 0 <= v i % v j < |v j| <= |v i| makes exactly the i-th summand shrink (sum_natAbs_update_emod_lt).

Base case: a primitive vector with a single nonzero coordinate must have that entry a unit (from exists w, w dot v = 1 collapsing to w k * v k = 1), so it already equals Pi.single k (v k) with IsUnit (v k) — A = 1.

Reaching EXACTLY e0 (not just a unit multiple c*e_k) is only true for n >= 2; in n = 1, SL1(Z)={1} fixes -e0 != e0 though both are primitive, so the unit-multiple form is the sharp general-n statement.

Sharpness of transitivity: SL₁(ℤ)={(1)} acts trivially (coe_sl_fin_one_eq_one via det_fin_one), so (1) and (-1) — both primitive — lie in DISTINCT orbits. SL₁(ℤ) has exactly 2 primitive-vector orbits vs a single orbit for n≥2. This proves the previously prose-only claim that the 1<n hypothesis in exists_sl_mulVec_eq_of_isPrimitive is genuinely necessary.

The parent file already had two primitivity reformulations (span=⊤, every-common-divisor-is-unit) but NOT the literal Finset.gcd=1 value nor the ring-theoretic IsCoprime form; both are cheap corollaries of isPrimitive_iff_forall_isUnit_of_dvd + Finset.gcd_dvd/dvd_gcd and Fin.sum_univ_two respectively.

Module.Basis is the current Mathlib name for the Basis type (moved into the Module namespace, Lean/Mathlib 4.26 module system); granular `import Mathlib.LinearAlgebra.StdBasis` does not re-export `Basis` to a non-module file — use `import Mathlib` + `open Module`.

SpecialLinearGroup.toLin A : (n→R) ≃ₗ[R] n→R gives the linear equivalence of a unimodular matrix directly (no Invertible-instance juggling); its action on the standard basis vector e_k extracts the k-th column via toLin_apply + Matrix.toLin_apply + mulVec_single_one.

The converse `member of a ℤ-basis ⇒ primitive` needs NO dimension hypothesis: the dual coordinate functional b.coord i is a ℤ-linear map ℤⁿ→ℤ sending b i to 1; representing it by its values w j = b.coord i (e_j) on the standard basis gives an explicit integer dual with w · (b i) = 1 (= primitivity). This even covers n=1 where SLₙ transitivity fails.

Orientation refinement: the n≥2 unimodular completion is not merely GLₙ(ℤ) (det ±1) but SLₙ(ℤ) (det +1) — slColumnBasis of an SL matrix has Basis.det = det ↑ₘA = 1, so every primitive vector extends to an ORIENTATION-PRESERVING basis. The SL/GL distinction is sharp only at n=1: (−1)∈ℤ¹ completes to the basis {(−1)} (det −1) but to NO det-+1 basis; det-1 completion exists iff v 0 = 1.

Saturation/pure-line criterion completes the module-theoretic triad: primitive v ⇔ ℤ·v is SATURATED (c•x∈ℤv ∧ c≠0 ⟹ x∈ℤv, i.e. ℤⁿ/ℤv torsion-free). This is the INTERNAL member — no auxiliary basis or complement — and the textbook working definition; sits below the direct-summand form (over a PID saturated⇒summand, but that structure theorem is unnecessary: both directions elementary).

Primitive ⇔ ℤⁿ/(ℤ·v) torsion-free (NoZeroSMulDivisors ℤ quotient) for v≠0 — canonical Mathlib-typeclass form of saturation, completing the internal characterization: quotient map converts NoZeroSMulDivisors field c•x̄=0→c=0∨x̄=0 into saturation via Submodule.Quotient.mk_eq_zero

Rank form of unimodular completion: for ANY nonzero v, finrank ℤ (ℤⁿ/ℤ·v) = n-1 (finrank_quotient_span_singleton) — no primitivity needed. Uses rank-nullity Submodule.finrank_quotient_add_finrank, valid over ℤ because IsDomain ⟹ HasRankNullity; the line ℤ·v is free of rank 1 via LinearEquiv.toSpanNonzeroSingleton + finrank_self, and Module.finrank_fin_fun gives finrank(Fin n→ℤ)=n. finrank is insensitive to torsion, so this holds even for non-primitive v.

Freeness is the exact locus of primitivity: IsPrimitive.free_quotient — for PRIMITIVE v the quotient ℤⁿ/ℤ·v is Module.Free ℤ, since it is Module.Finite (quotient of finite) and torsion-free (NoZeroSMulDivisors via isPrimitive_iff_noZeroSMulDivisors_quotient), firing the PID structure instance Module.free_of_finite_type_torsion_free. Non-primitive nonzero v: same finrank n-1 but has torsion, NOT free.

Capstone IsPrimitive.quotientEquiv_fin: for primitive v, ℤⁿ/(ℤ·v) ≃ₗ[ℤ] ℤ^(n-1), built from free+finrank via Module.finBasisOfFinrankEq ℤ _ hrank |>.equivFun — the coordinate-free numerical face of unimodular completion.

Sharp boundary of isPrimitive_iff_noZeroSMulDivisors_quotient: the torsion of ℤⁿ/(ℤ·v) for non-primitive nonzero v is CYCLIC ℤ/(content), generated by the primitive-part class [v/gcd], degenerating to 0 exactly at content=1. Quantifies non-primitivity by an explicit torsion witness of exact order = content.

Proof engine: v=d•p with p primitive⟹p≠0; smul_left_injective cancels p in c•p=(k·d)•p to force c=k·d; primitivity of p via gcd criterion (d·e ∣ gcd(v)=d ⟹ e unit). No Smith-normal-form / structure theorem needed — all elementary, 0-axiom.
